en: GS - As you surely know, Lord Draupnir, strict neutrality is Bifrost's founding principle. However much Grand Duke Mozel favours Pandragon, public opinion in Bifrost will be against it.

Draupnir - I'm not asking the Bifrost army to attack Trisys. A show of force on the Trisys border alone would split the Trisys army in two. Given Grand Duke Mozel's sympathies, I think it's possible, don't you?
GS - In any case, I'll do my best. I have many friends among the scouts in Bifrost, Strider for one, so we may get a better result than expected.

Draupnir - One thing is certain: a chance like this, with Trisys isolated, does not come often. But desert warfare may work heavily against us. Hardly anyone in the expedition has fought in the desert, so success in Trisys may depend on you.

GS - I've heard that Kassim, the King of the Desert, is a fearsome man. Our Silver Arrow troops have little battle experience overall; it will be hard for them to show their true strength in the desert.

Draupnir - Above all, I worry that hot-blooded Prince Daicus of Dagal or young Erich of Astania will act rashly. That makes your role all the more important... Take the mercenaries left in Dagal and set out at once.
